subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: What ACP skill-context contract should OpenClaw support for `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")`?
rationale: The code can carry rendered context, but maintainers must choose the permanent selection mode, redaction/audit boundary, default/config behavior, and how this relates to broader harness skill parity before implementation is safe.

options.title: Narrow explicit/default contract
options.body: Add explicit skill ids and an optional configured default set with redaction/audit metadata, while deferring automatic relevance detection until observability and security behavior are proven.

options.title: Defer to harness parity work
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until #95058 settles a shared skill prompt contract across native, Codex, and ACP harnesses.

options.title: Keep ACP isolated
options.body: Document that ACP children must use their own harness-native skill mechanisms or explicit task text, and reject OpenClaw skill injection for now.

recommendation.title: Narrow explicit/default contract
recommendation.body: Add explicit skill ids and an optional configured default set with redaction/audit metadata, while deferring automatic relevance detection until observability and security behavior are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the related harness skill-contract issue that overlaps the product boundary this ACP decision must align with.
